L9: # Title:On the Suboptimality of Rate--Distortion-Optimal Compression: Fundamental Accuracy Limits for Distributed Localization
L10: 
L11: Authors:【5†Amir Weiss】

L13: View a PDF of the paper titled On the Suboptimality of Rate--Distortion-Optimal Compression: Fundamental Accuracy Limits for Distributed Localization, by Amir Weiss
L14: 
L15: 【6†View PDF】 【7†HTML (experimental)】
L16: > Abstract:We derive fundamental accuracy limits for distributed localization when a fusion center has access only to independently rate-distortion (RD)-optimally compressed versions of multi-sensor observations, under a line-of-sight propagation model with a Gaussian wideband waveform. Using the Gaussian RD test-channel model together with a Whittle spectral Fisher-information characterization, we obtain an explicit frequency-domain Cramér-Rao lower bound.
L17: A two-band, two-level specialization yields closed-form expressions and reveals a rate-induced regime change: RD-optimal compression under a squared-error distortion measure can eliminate localization-informative spectral content. A simple band-selective scheme can outperform RD compression by orders of magnitude at the same rate, motivating localization-aware compression for networked sensing and integrated sensing and communication systems.

L0@P0: GEOMETRY-ADAPTIVE DATA COMPRESSION FOR TDOA/FDOA LOCATION
L1@P0: Mo Chen and Mark L. Fowler
L2@P0: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
L3@P0: State University of New York at Binghamton
L4@P0: {mchen0, mfowler}@Binghamton.edu
L5@P0: ABSTRACT
L6@P0: The location of an emitting target is estimated by intercepting its
L7@P0: emitted signal and sharing them among several sensors to
L8@P0: measure the time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) and the
L9@P0: frequency-difference-of-arrival (FDOA). Doing this in a timely
L10@P0: and energy efficient fashion, which is especially important for
L11@P0: wireless sensor network applications, requires effective data
L12@P0: compression. Since the commonly used MSE distortion measure
L13@P0: is only weakly related to optimal TDOA/FDOA estimation, in
L14@P0: this paper, we derive a new class of non-MSE distortion
L15@P0: measures for TDOA/FDOA estimation using the concept of
L16@P0: Fisher information. We then use these new distortion measures
L17@P0: to compress the data using a wavelet packet transform and show
L18@P0: that it improves TDOA/FDOA estimation accuracies relative to
L19@P0: using the MSE-based compression. Finally, the scheme of
L20@P0: applying our algorithms in a wireless sensor network is
L21@P0: proposed, and energy efficiency and accuracy enhancement of
L22@P0: the proposed scheme over that of traditional scheme using MSE
L23@P0: is shown through the simulations.
L24@P0: 1. INTRODUCTION
L25@P0: A common way to locate an electromagnetic emitter is to
L26@P0: measure the time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) and the
L27@P0: frequency-difference-of-arrival (FDOA) between signals
L28@P0: received at pairs of sensors [1],[2]. This requires that the
L29@P0: samples of one signal are sent over a data link, where data
L30@P0: compression can reduce latency and save energy. Some past
L31@P0: results are available on the issue of compression for
L32@P0: TDOA/FDOA applications [3]ñ[7], but only recently have
L33@P0: researchers begun to explore other than the standard meansquare-error (MSE) distortion measure [5]ñ[7]. We introduced a
L34@P0: new non-MSE distortion measure [5] that uses a CRLB-based
L35@P0: measure for the TDOA-only problem. However, we have found
L36@P0: [5] that optimizing this measure was difficult because the form
L37@P0: that the CRLB-based distortion metric takes depends on the
L38@P0: relationships between the SNRs at the two sensors.
L39@P0: More recently we have shown [6] that a Fisher-informationbased approach avoids these difficulties and we developed a
L40@P0: general method for a single-parameter problem. A key
L41@P0: advantage for this approach is that if the noise is uncorrelated
L42@P0: between sensors, then the total Fisher information is the sum of
L43@P0: the Fisher information from each sensor. Compression only
L44@P0: impacts one sensor so we can avoid the complicating crosssensor couplings.
L45@P0: In this paper we attack the two-parameter TDOA/FDOA
L46@P0: problem by extending our single-parameter ideas [6] and explore
L47@P0: trade-off issues that arise. We assume that the TDOA/FDOA
L48@P0: estimation processing and compression processing are not jointly
L49@P0: designed ñ this is motivated by our belief that sensors are likely
L50@P0: be called to provide data to other processing systems that are
L51@P0: independently designed. With our proposed compression
L52@P0: scheme, we develop a new cooperative scheme for the sensor
L53@P0: nodes in the wireless sensor network to adapt the compression
L54@P0: scheme to the sensor-target geometry.

L91@P0: The FIM specifies an information ellipse ñ the larger the better ñ
L92@P0: with semi-axes along the FIMís eigenvectors and whose lengths
L93@P0: are the square roots of the eigenvalues.
L94@P0: Lossy compression of the data vector x changes the FIM.
L95@P0: Namely, it reduces the on-diagonal elements ii J , which makes
L96@P0: the post-compression information ellipse smaller; it is unclear
L97@P0: what effect it would have on the cross-information and hence the
L98@P0: tilt of the ellipse. In the single-parameter case [6] the way to
L99@P0: proceed was clear: compress so as to minimize the reduction in
L100@P0: J11 for a given bit budget. But how should we proceed in the
L101@P0: two-parameter case? There are several possibilities, but our
L102@P0: choice is to minimize the impact on the information ellipseís
L103@P0: semi-axis lengths while neglecting the impact on the ellipseís
L104@P0: tilt: this implies minimizing the reduction of the FIMís
L105@P0: eigenvalues. A simple, effective measure is to minimize the
L106@P0: reduction of the sum of the eigenvalues, which is equivalent to
L107@P0: minimizing the reduction of the trace of the FIM. However,
L108@P0: sometimes TDOA accuracy is more important than FDOA
L109@P0: accuracy, or vice versa; so, we use a weighted trace. Thus, our
L110@P0-1: goal is to seek an operational rate-distortion method that minimizes the reduction in αJ11 + (1-α)J22 with 0 ≤ α ≤ 1 while
L111@P1: satisfying a budget on the total number of bits.
